beats: Hook: your chip's CNOT runs only one way, control on A and target on B; the program needs it the other way round; no new hardware (line_qc_rewire_lead_mover: the mover always leads). Cast for lecture Q25-06 (QC05-05, QC05-06): the planner (bun with a pencil, cardigan) is the compiler; the mover (flat cap, waistcoat) is the hardware.

CZ flips the sign only when both qubits are 1, and it is symmetric: it does not care which qubit is which, like a high five (Q25-06 17:40-21:20; the recipe: action on basis states -> matrix -> check unitary, 20:33-21:02; line_qc_rewire_high_five).

CZ = (I x H) CNOT (I x H): seen through the X-basis lenses on the target, a flip becomes a sign (21:20-29:13; Q24-05 29:20-30:56; reuse line_qc_hbridge_two_glasses and line_qc_hbridge_cake_turntable from QC05-02).

Four Hadamards reverse a CNOT: twirl both partners and the follower leads (29:13-32:18; line_qc_rewire_lead_mover -> line_qc_rewire_twirl -> line_qc_rewire_lead_planner, the cover idea). Why bother: on some chips one direction is the native, easier one (clip 32:44-33:35; Q24-05 31:24-33:40; phrase it generally, as FACTS.md allows).

SWAP = three CNOTs, exactly the classical in-place XOR swap that needs no spare variable (34:12-45:16, clip 38:41-39:08; Q24-05 36:38-41:44; line_qc_rewire_fishbowl_swap: the everyday way needs a spare bowl; the XOR rows of bits are lettered).
Linearity: check an identity on the basis states and it holds for every superposition (44:13-45:07; code only).

Partial equivalence: when the compiler knows an input is still |0>, a SWAP needs only two CNOTs: a bowl known to be empty takes one pour (45:16-51:13, clip 47:39-48:32; line_qc_rewire_fish_pour). Compilers track untouched |0> qubits.
SWAP is "classical": together with single-qubit gates it can never create entanglement; swapping seats does not mix what each one holds (51:13-52:53; Q24-05 49:14-51:36; line_qc_rewire_bench_swap).
Never caption her 2024 remark that two iSWAPs make a SWAP (iSWAP^2 = Z x Z).
Cover (line_cover_qc05_05; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the planner twirls the mover under a raised arm on an empty dance floor.
